original.prompt: In September 2026, India ordered 112 coal-fired captive power plants to maximise generation from October to December and sell surplus electricity to the grid. Consider the following statements in this context:
items: The order covers plants supplying industries such as steel mills and aluminium smelters.
Weaker rainfall reduced hydroelectric generation, forcing coal plants to compensate.
Nighttime electricity shortages in September 2026 were lower than the shortfalls of the preceding summer.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 3 is wrong. Nighttime shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding the summer shortfalls. Earlier, in March, disrupted gas supplies had prompted preparations to force imported-coal plants to raise generation.
original.source: Nighttime electricity shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding this year’s summer shortfalls.

rewritten.prompt: In September 2026, India ordered 112 coal-fired captive power plants to maximise generation from October to December and sell surplus electricity to the grid. Consider the following statements in this context:
items: The order covers plants supplying industries such as steel mills and aluminium smelters.
Weaker rainfall reduced hydroelectric generation, forcing coal plants to compensate.
Nighttime electricity shortages in September 2026 exceeded the shortfalls of the preceding summer.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct: the order covers plants supplying steel mills and aluminium smelters, weaker rainfall cut hydroelectric output, and nighttime shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding the summer shortfalls. Power-station coal stocks also fell 24% between end-August and 26 September, leaving roughly seven days' supply.
rewritten.source: Nighttime electricity shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding this year’s summer shortfalls.
